title: Register Erasure Run
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, choose a register $r$, states $c_R,c_E,\mathrm{next}$, and suppose that in state $c_R$ every transition is the prescribed register action, in state $c_E$ every transition is the prescribed erasing action, and neither state is an oracle-call state. For any configuration $c$ and Boolean word $w$, for every $k\le |w|$, starting in state $c_E$ with register $r$ containing the prefix of $w$ of length $k$ and its head at position $k-1$, after $k+1$ steps the machine is in state $\mathrm{next}$ with register $r$ blank and its head at zero, while the rest of the configuration is as in $c$. At every earlier time $t<k+1$, the configuration has state $c_E$ and some tape contents and head position $q$ for register $r$ satisfying $-1\le q\le k-1$.
